title: Fleet Availability and Utilization
body: ADW's core fleet is mostly fit to work: excavators ran 96% available against 79% usage and trucks 95% against 74% in the 10-Sep weekly figures. That gap is production lost by operations, not maintenance. It is also what Maaden's 80% utilization escalation is aimed at.
keyPoints: Read availability and utilization as a pair. High availability with low utilization means dispatch, sequencing or face access, so fix it on shift. Low availability means a workshop problem. The two need different people and different fixes.

The 80% target needs 19.2 productive hours a day, and the site is running 16–17. Most of the 2–3 hours to recover sits in two lines: meal break (2.0 hrs) and "others" (1.0 hr). Tramming, blasting, pre-use, survey and fuelling add up to only about 1 hour.
"Others" is not a reason. If standby gets logged as "others", "no job" or "truck shortage" without a root cause, the delay breakdown Kangwa asked for can't be produced.
Say which denominator you are using. Counting 21 active trucks gives about 96% availability. Counting all 24 gives 80–85%. Leadership will challenge the flattering number.
Use the best trucks in the fleet as the benchmark. Some trucks idle 6–6.5 hrs a shift while the best run 2.5–3 hrs. The best trucks show what is achievable; the worst show where the losses are.
apply: EX-253 and EX-123 are both down, so trucks will bunch at the remaining faces. Get supervisors to log each below-85% hour in the hourly productivity log and to split each "truck shortage" into dispatch, mechanical or operator.
